answer: In a sonnet contest using lotus and sparrow as prompts, each vote needs a badge from one synchronized, in-person ceremony. Observers keep attendees present through a shared voting window and issue one signed badge per person. Validators count each badge once across all accounts. New keys cannot multiply badges; another vote requires recruiting another person to attend. Colluders can still buy participation, and dishonest observers can issue extra badges, so admission checks remain a trust assumption.
